title: Clock booster: when stopping time helps
summary: The Clock stops the level timer, which helps execution-heavy attempts but does not repair a blocked route or a mismatched board.
effect: The Clock booster stops the active level timer; this behavior is described by players on the official App Store listing.
useWhen: You already know the correct block order but need more execution time to complete it.
The remaining routes are open and the countdown, rather than board space, is the only immediate failure risk.
A replay consistently reaches the same solvable final phase with too little time left.
avoidWhen: The opening board does not match the guide or you have not identified the correct exits.
Blocks are already locked behind a bad sequence; stopping time does not create board space.
You are still experimenting with the opening and cannot explain which moves the extra time will enable.
decisionChecks: Confirm the board variant and planned move order.
Separate a timing failure from a routing failure.
Use the Clock only when the remaining sequence is known and physically open.
Restart instead when the board is already soft-locked.
